Definition: from a compound of G1909 and G757 (meaning a governor of a district, "eparch"); a special region of government, i.e. a Roman præfecture:--province.
BiblicalUsage: Eparchia is a province, a Roman district under a governor — the word appears when the governor asks Paul what province he is from, and when Festus arrives in his province. It is the language of empire, of borders and rulers and who answers to whom.
TheologicalSignificance: Paul's trial moves through Roman provinces while a higher court is really in session, and I believe God works through the empire's machinery rather than being stopped by it.
RelatedEvents: Paul Before Felix, Festus, and Agrippa
